data.title: TKG AIKANG Backs Second Tender Offer as Parent Seeks Full Control and Delisting
data.description:
TKG AIKANG CO. LTD ( (KR:022220) ) has issued an update.

TKG AIKANG CO. LTD’s board has issued a formal opinion on a second tender offer by its controlling shareholder, TKG TAEKWANG CO. LTD, which aims to acquire the remaining 31.04% stake and delist the company from KOSDAQ. The KRW 900 per-share offer matches the first tender round and, based on prior external valuation and recent trading data, is deemed an appropriate price to give ordinary investors a realistic exit from an illiquid stock.

The board expresses support for the implementation of the tender offer but adopts a neutral stance on whether individual shareholders should tender, stressing that decisions depend on each investor’s objectives, return expectations, liquidity needs and tax situation. It notes that the offeror has secured cash funding, will purchase all tendered shares, and has pledged post-delisting measures such as market and off-market buybacks and potential corporate actions to protect minority shareholders and facilitate future exits.

data.title: Skanska invests EUR 66M in sustainable Nowy Format office project in Kraków
data.description:
An announcement from Skanska AB ( ($SE:SKA.B) ) is now available.

Skanska is expanding its sustainable office portfolio in Central Europe with a major new project in Kraków, Poland, reinforcing its role as a leading global construction and project development group. The company continues to focus on environmentally certified, tenant-friendly office buildings that align with EU Taxonomy criteria and broader decarbonization goals.

Skanska will invest about EUR 66 million, roughly SEK 720 million, in the first phase of the Nowy Format office complex, booking a PLN 140 million construction contract in Europe in the third quarter of 2026. The initial nine-storey building, Nowy Format A1, will provide 21,400 square meters of leasable space, extensive gardens and terraces, and operate without connection to the city heating network, relying on heat pumps and 100 percent renewable electricity.
